Computer vision

Bey Scanner

Point a camera at a stadium. It watches the spin and stops the clock itself.

Place the bey in the stadium, start the spin and hold the camera steady. The scanner samples many frames and ends the stamina timer when rotation stops.

How I Code

Real samples from my projects.

I'm Santiago Rojas.

I design and build software, and I want to become an AI engineer.

Why AI

AI is the first technology that changed what I personally could build. Ideas that used to stop at a sketch now become working apps that real people can use. Once you have felt that, you want to know exactly how it works.

Alfred is where it became serious for me. Getting a language model, speech recognition and a natural voice to run privately on my own laptop taught me more than any tutorial could. I had to think about memory limits, response times, and what an assistant should never be allowed to do.

I don't want to only call other people's models. I want to understand them: how they are trained, why they fail, and how to make them small, fast and trustworthy enough for people to depend on.

Where I'm heading

I'm still learning, and I'm doing it by shipping. I'm building my Python foundations while putting real projects in front of real people and listening when they tell me what isn't good enough. The goal is to become an engineer who can take an AI idea from research to something a person actually uses every day.

What I care about

Private by default

Alfred runs on your own machine. Your conversations don't have to leave it.

Honest about limits

If something is a demo, it says so. If a feature wasn't tested, I say that too.

Finish things

An idea only counts once someone else can download it and use it.
